title: Form-state pseudo-classes
learningObjectives: Explain form-state pseudo-classes and write selectors that match the intended elements.

understand.concept: Form-state pseudo-classes select controls based on interaction and validity state. Examples include :required, :optional, :valid, :invalid, :checked, :disabled, :enabled, :read-only, :read-write, and :placeholder-shown. They allow feedback styles to follow native control state.
understand.whyItMatters: State styling can help users understand forms, but colour alone is not enough. Pair visual cues with labels and clear text messages, and avoid marking an untouched field as an error before the user has had a chance to interact where that would be confusing.
understand.analogy: A form-state selector is like a status light that responds to the actual state of a control.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; selector matching and specificity follow the CSS selector and cascade rules.

explain.narrative: The email field receives invalid styling after a non-empty invalid value is entered and valid styling when the browser considers it valid.

examples.code: <form class='signup'><label>Email <input type='email' required placeholder='name@example.com'></label><label><input type='checkbox' required> I agree</label><button>Submit</button></form><style>.signup{display:grid;gap:1rem;max-width:24rem}.signup input:invalid:not(:placeholder-shown){border:2px solid #b42318}.signup input:valid{border:2px solid #18704a}.signup input:focus-visible{outline:3px solid #245b48;outline-offset:2px}</style>
examples.explanation: The email field receives invalid styling after a non-empty invalid value is entered and valid styling when the browser considers it valid.
examples.expectedOutput: The browser applies the styles to elements that match the selectors.

practise.guidedTask: Add styles for required, disabled, checked, and valid controls. Ensure every state is understandable without colour alone.
practise.independentTask: Create a small document with several matching and non-matching elements. Write selectors for the required states and verify them in developer tools.
hints: Inspect which elements match each selector.
Keep selectors readable and tied to stable semantics.

questions.prompt: Which pseudo-class matches a form control whose value passes its constraint validation?
questions.explanation: :valid matches a control that satisfies its constraint validation.

questions.prompt: What is a good way to verify a complex selector?
options: Inspect the matched elements and computed styles
Assume the selector matches every element
questions.answer: Inspect the matched elements and computed styles
questions.explanation: Inspecting the actual match set and computed styles confirms how the selector behaves.
